subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 44-year-old man is found to have more than 60 adenomatous colonic polyps on screening colonoscopy. Genetic testing shows biallelic pathogenic variants in MUTYH, which encodes a DNA glycosylase, and no APC mutation is identified.
question: A deficiency of which of the following steps is most directly responsible for the accumulation of DNA damage in this patient?

options.text: Excision of a bulky oligonucleotide containing thymine dimers
Cleavage of the 5' end of the AP site by an endonuclease
Filling of the gap by DNA polymerase beta
Sealing of the nick by DNA ligase
Removal of an altered base to create an apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) site

explanation_correct: In base excision repair, a base-specific glycosylase removes the altered base and creates an AP site; AP endonuclease and AP lyase then remove the backbone segment, DNA polymerase beta fills the gap, and ligase seals it. Loss of the glycosylase MUTYH impairs removal of oxidized bases and causes MUTYH-associated polyposis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Excision of bulky, helix-distorting lesions such as thymine dimers is performed by nucleotide excision repair.
explanation_incorrect.B: AP endonuclease acts after the AP site has been created, so it is not the initiating defect here.
explanation_incorrect.C: Polymerase beta fills the gap later in base excision repair; it is not the enzyme encoded by MUTYH.
explanation_incorrect.D: DNA ligase seals the nick at the final step of base excision repair.

educationalObjective: Base excision repair begins when a base-specific glycosylase removes the altered base and creates an AP site.
